summary: This video conducts a massive quantitative backtest of over 100,000 price action strategy variations across nearly five years of 1-minute NQ and ES futures data (327 million simulated trades) using Claude to generate the backtesting infrastructure. The study evaluates ten classic price action concepts across multiple timeframes (1m to Daily), accounting for real commissions, slippage, and out-of-sample locked data testing. The results demonstrate that higher timeframes (4-hour and Daily) outperform lower timeframes, flip zones provide the strongest support/resistance edge, hard stops outperform close-based stops, and the 4-hour 'Change of Character' reversal strategy without liquidity sweeps generated the most consistent out-of-sample profits ($62,179 on NQ and $39,284 on ES per contract over two locked years).

key_points: Tested over 100,000 price action trading strategy variations using Claude to write code.
Backtest used 5 years of 1-minute futures data for NQ (Nasdaq) and ES (S&P 500), totaling 3.6 million bars and 327 million simulated trades.
Author credentials: Math and Economics degree at UCLA, 3+ years in investment banking at Raymond James, and 2 years building automated trading systems for clients.
Price action relies on trading chart structure directly: support/resistance levels, trend (break of structure), change of character (CHoCH), sweeps, and confirmation candles.
Change of Character (CHoCH) represents the first time price breaks structural trend in the opposite direction (e.g., closing below a higher low in an uptrend).
Sweeps occur when price briefly exceeds a high or low to trigger stop losses before reversing; backtest data shows sweeps reverse only about half the time.
Tested across six chart timeframes: 1m, 5m, 15m, 1h, 4h, and daily.

segments.topic: The Ten Core Price Action Setups Tested
key_points: Tested 10 core price action setups: Level bounce, Breakout, Flip zone, Trend pullback, Trend line, Break of structure, Change of character, Sweep and reclaim, Supply and demand, Fair value gap.
Quantified subjective 'eye-drawn' chart decisions into explicit parameter 'dials': touch count, line vs zone, confirmation style, stop loss location, profit target, timeframe, and context filters.
Total theoretical search space encompasses 20.3 trillion possible parameter combinations.
Backtested 40,000 baseline versions (4,000 per setup) plus 61,345 common trader setups, totaling 101,345 strategy variations.
Applied a strict 'gauntlet' test: $4 round-trip commission + 1 tick slippage per stop/market order, ambiguous candles (where high/low hit stop and target in same 1-min bar) treated as losses.
Locked away 2 full years of ES/NQ data for strict out-of-sample validation.
Out of 101,345 tested versions: 88,986 generated enough trades (>=30) to evaluate.
24,879 versions were net profitable after accounting for trading costs in discovery.
8,310 versions achieved a Sharpe ratio of 0.5 or higher (~8% of total tested versions).
Claims of 80%+ win rates in price action trading are rarely supported by data; win rate has low correlation (0.27) with actual profit.
On 1-minute charts, transaction costs consume 46.0% of gross profits, compared to only 3.9% on daily charts.
Trading higher timeframes (1h, 4h, Daily) makes achieving profitability significantly easier due to reduced friction per trade.

segments.topic: Level Rules: Touches and Flip Zones
key_points: Real support/resistance levels held 51.1% of touches vs 42.4% for random lines (+8.7 pts NQ, +8.5 pts ES).
A level touched 4 times held no better (+6.1 pts over random) than a level touched once (+9.0 pts over random). Levels touched 3+ times bounced less and broke through more often.
Flip zones (old resistance turning into new support) were the single strongest level rule, holding +11.5 percentage points better than random on NQ and +10.9 points on ES.
Break of structure (-0.04 ATR) and Change of Character (-0.05 ATR) on their own do not move price predictably.
Among all trend setups, only Change of Character (CHoCH) reversal achieved a positive median profit (+$61).
CHoCH setups without a preceding liquidity sweep made +$903/year vs -$834/year with a sweep.

segments.topic: Confirmation, Stops, Context, and Multi-Market Tests
key_points: Waiting for candle confirmation vs limit order at touch: limit lost -$1,093/year while confirmation lost -$373/year (a +$719/year improvement in edge, despite giving up 4.3 points of entry).
Hard stops (-$158/yr) outperformed close-based stops (-$290/yr), saving $132/year.
Filtering for New York session only (8am-4pm ET) added +$270/year; skipping trades into a 3+ day directional run added +$246/year.
In consistency tests across both NQ and ES, only the 4-hour Change of Character setup passed on both markets in both setup groups.
In the 2-year locked out-of-sample dataset (which included a 22.5% market selloff and 74.5% rally): 9.2% of 1m versions were profitable vs 45.1% of 4h versions.

The best overall strategy variation (4h CHoCH, no sweep, enter at close, hard stop at previous swing, 1:1 risk-reward) generated +$62,179 on NQ and +$39,284 on ES per contract over the 2 locked years with 61 NQ trades and 54% win rate.
66% of all 314 common 4h CHoCH versions made money on NQ and 54.5% made money on ES.

segments.topic: 7 Key Rules That Survived & Market Insights
key_points: Seven rules survived testing: 1. 4h Change of Character; 2. Higher chart timeframes; 3. New York session only; 4. Skip trades into 3+ day run; 5. Confirmation candle on NQ; 6. Hard stops; 7. No sweep before CHoCH.
Across 9,000 strategy tests, ICT backtests, and Price Action backtests, mean-reversion/reversal strategies consistently represent the core edge in futures markets.

segments.topic: Prompt Architecture for Replicating in Claude
key_points: Provided 5 modular prompts to build the backtesting stack in Python with Claude: Prompt 1 (Data & Dials), Prompt 2 (Engine & Level Tests), Prompt 3 (The Funnel), Prompt 4 (The Final Test), Prompt 5 (The Dashboard).

claims.claim: Price action trading strategies reliably achieve 80%+ win rates.
claims.caveats: Only 138 out of 40,000 tested strategies reached an 80%+ win rate, and win rate had a very low correlation (0.27) with overall profitability.

claims.claim: Real price action support and resistance levels hold significantly better than random lines.
claims.caveats: Real levels held 51.1% of touches compared to 42.4% for random lines (+8.7 pts NQ, +8.5 pts ES), but touching a level 3+ times slightly decreased its hold probability.

claims.claim: Flip zones (resistance turning into support) are the strongest level concept in price action.
claims.caveats: Held +11.5 percentage points better than random on NQ and +10.9 points on ES across out-of-sample tests.

claims.claim: Waiting for candle confirmation improves net trading edge over entering at the level touch.
claims.caveats: Gives up 4.3 points of price entry, but reduces net annual loss by +$719 on NQ.

claims.claim: Hard stop losses outperform close-based candle stops.
claims.caveats: Close-based stops achieved a higher win rate (40% vs 29%), but average losses were substantially larger, costing $132 more per year.

claims.claim: Higher timeframes (4h/Daily) drastically outperform lower timeframes (1m/5m) for price action.
claims.caveats: Transaction costs consume 46% of gross profit on 1m charts versus 3.9% on daily charts. 45% of 4h strategy versions were profitable out-of-sample vs 9% on 1m.

strategies.name: 4h Change of Character (CHoCH) Reversal Strategy
strategies.logic: Reversal trading system that enters when a 4-hour candle closes past the prior swing structure (higher low in an uptrend or lower high in a downtrend), signaling a shift in trend direction without requiring a preceding liquidity sweep.
entry_rules: Identify 4-hour trend structure (higher highs and higher lows).
Wait for a 4-hour candle to close past the previous swing low (CHoCH).
Do NOT require a liquidity sweep before the change of character.
Enter at the candle close upon confirmation (NQ).
exit_rules: Place a hard stop loss at the previous swing high (for short) or swing low (for long).
Set take profit target at 1:1 risk-to-reward ratio matching the stop loss distance.

parameters.value: New York Session only (8:00 AM - 4:00 PM ET)

parameters.name: Run Filter
parameters.value: Skip trades into a 3+ day directional run

parameters.name: Stop Loss Type
